title: a test run reaches a TESTING database, never the live one
intention: Under a test run (the process carries CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID) every write the store door makes lands in `cairn_testing`, never in `cairn`: store.write, a scratch table minted, the owner and scratch registries, ensure_database. Reads are not redirected: under a test run store.query reads live, except a table the run itself created in cairn_testing, which it reads there (outline 4.3.1.5.1.5.2 clause 4: testing first, live underneath). Live is read under a test run only through a read-only connection, so a proof can read live and cannot write it. Without a test id nothing changes: `cairn`.
why: Akien 2026-11-14 (relayed by the orchestrator, answering Q#104): "we need a TESTING database." The lived symptoms are all from proofs and scratch tables sharing the live `cairn` database: (1) 2026-09-06, 9,087 tables, 12 live (201a37bf1613); (2) 2026-11-14 on akiendell, a sweep that read live processes as dead dropped the caller's own scratch tables, and 36 orphan seal_ann_*_delivery tables stood in the live database (5b940b1c4fbe, 9484180b4ff4); (3) the sweep is a DELETE FROM over a registry in the live database, run by a test, so a bug in a test-run's sweep is a bug against live tables. Separation by database is physics (Postgres cannot read across databases on one connection), not a naming convention that a pattern sweep must respect.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics), Law 6 (a test run owns nothing live), the standing rule that a test against live data is marked as testing.
how: D1: store.database_name() reads CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID (set -> `cairn_testing`, unset -> DB_NAME); every connection that can write (connect() as used by write, the scratch mint and sweep, the registries, ensure_database) dials it. D2: under a test id, store.query routes per table: a table present in cairn_testing (one the run created) is read there; any other is read through a live connection opened with default_transaction_read_only=on, so an INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL through it raises. Without a test id store.query is unchanged. D3 of the cast (a live-reading proof gets no door) is dropped: Akien's Q112 answer says a proof may read live. The row-grain overlay pinned at the run's start seq (clause 4's full form) is measured in the build's census, not built here: the overlay here is at table grain. D4: the proof, one tooth per outcome.

out: the bus and every other component (they reach the database through the store door, and the environment variable they already carry picks the database)

measured.saw: store.DB_NAME = 'cairn' is the one database every connect() dials; scratch tables, the owner registry cairn_owned and the scratch registry cairn_scratch all live in it; the tester marks a run with CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID (runs.py:37) and the bus launch already carries it to the bus process (remote.py:240)
akiendell's live `cairn` database held 32 tables, 24 of them leaked seal_ann_*_delivery debris from tests (36 after one more run), before 5b940b1c4fbe

UNMEASURED: how many proofs in the corpus read or write LIVE (non-scratch) tables and so change behaviour under the testing database; the build's census over the corpus is its first step and is listed in the ticket's measured
built at testing-db @601f62f23: test_db_domain.py asserted current_database() == store.DB_NAME and reds under a marked run; one line to store.database_name() is green marked and unmarked

Akien answered Q#112 (open-087b17d58fb9): a proof MAY read the live database; test writes stay out of live (the TESTING database, or marked as testing artifacts the rest of the system ignores). The branch @bc6c1bb2f built option (a), a test sees only testing, so it needs rework to allow live reads before it crosses; the rework is parked while the fleet's usage pace holds
measured.how: his answer, relayed verbatim by orchestrator; outline 4.3.1.5.1.5.1

measured.saw: The rework's shape is CC's TESTING-db design at outline 4.3.1.5.1.5.2 (Akien handed the mechanism to CC on 2026-11-14). The db proxy (the store door db_domain until the proxy exists) routes by session context. The test runner sets context=testing, never the proof. Testing writes go to the TESTING db from a reserved address range. Testing reads overlay testing rows on live, pinned at the run's start seq. Live context never consults testing. Rows carry a run id, are dropped at run end, and the sleep cycle sweeps orphans. The branch @bc6c1bb2f (testing-only reads) is reworked to this; still parked under the pace
Akien stamped the rework shape at outline 4.3.1.5.1.5.2 -amm ("4.3.1.5.1.5.2 -amm"); it is his call now. The rework stays parked under the usage pace only
measured.how: his words, relayed verbatim by orchestrator 2026-11-14

measured.saw: as cast, D1 redirected every connection under a test run, reads included, and D3 gave a live-reading proof no door: that contradicts Akien's Q112 answer (open-087b17d58fb9: "i see no reason why a proof can't read a live db") and outline 4.3.1.5.1.5.2 clause (4). Amended: writes to cairn_testing, reads live (read-only) except tables the run created; D3 dropped. a scratch table minted under a test id exists in cairn_testing and NOT in the live database; and sweep_scratch() under a test id leaves a scratch table and registry row standing in the live database
a table written through store.write by a process under a test id lands in cairn_testing, owner registry included, and the live database's owner registry is unchanged

under a test id, store.query of a live table the run has not created returns the live rows (a count equals the count read without a test id), and an INSERT sent through that read path raises a read-only error; the live row count is unchanged across the tooth
under a test id, a table the run created through store.write is read by store.query from cairn_testing (its rows, not live's), and the live database holds no table of that name
